amount_at_risk: Hub pool 11,548,584.08 ATOM; Osmosis pool 63,780,813.94 OSMO
description: Neither chain has a post-passage timelock parameter in its governance module. A passed proposal executes at EndBlock on passage (or at its scheduled upgrade height for software upgrades). The voting period (7 days Cosmos Hub, 5 days Osmosis; 3 days / 1 day expedited) is the only delay between a vote closing and funds moving or code activating. A passed community-pool spend therefore moves funds immediately, with no window for a second look, a veto by an external guardian, or an operator opt-out.
remediation: Governance proposal to add an execution delay for treasury spends and upgrades (a timelock module or a mandatory delay parameter in the gov module), with the delay published in gov params. Re-check: rerun fetch_treasury.py and confirm a timelock parameter appears in gov params and that proposals-cosmoshub.json / proposals-osmosis.json record a non-zero post_passage_execution_timelock_s.
title: No post-passage execution timelock on either chain

description: The votes endpoint returns an empty list for every finalized proposal checked (Cosmos Hub 1060 and 1058; Osmosis 1057), on two independent LCD providers and both gov v1 and v1beta1, while it returns full vote lists for proposals still in their voting period (865, 497, and 506 votes). Independent per-voter verification of passed proposals — who voted, with how much stake — is therefore impossible from public LCD data alone; only the aggregate tally survives.
remediation: Publish per-vote records for finalized proposals through a public indexer or an archived endpoint, and record the archive URL in the proposal metadata. Re-check: rerun audit_proposals.py and confirm votes_fetched > 0 for finalized proposals.
title: Per-vote records for finalized proposals are not retrievable from public LCDs

description: Proposal 1060 states the recipient is a 4-of-6 DAODAO multisig, but the threshold cannot be confirmed from on-chain account state via the public LCD: the auth module returns a BaseAccount with no pubkey and sequence 0 (expected for a CosmWasm contract account), and CosmWasm smart-contract queries (threshold, list_voters) against the contract return HTTP 500 from this LCD. The contract itself exists on-chain (code_id 179, created at block 33,506,400, admin is itself), but its voter set and threshold were not retrievable here. The 4-of-6 claim therefore rests on the proposal text alone.
remediation: Publish the multisig's voter set and threshold from the contract state (e.g. a DAODAO page link or a contract-query result) in the proposal's forum thread, and require future multisig mandates to include a verifiable contract-state citation. Re-check: query the contract's threshold from an LCD that serves wasm smart queries and compare with the proposal text.
title: USDC migration multisig threshold is not independently verifiable from the public LCD

description: Proposal 1060 sent 566,067.055810 USDC.n from the community pool to the migration multisig. The pool no longer holds any USDC.n (denom ibc/F663521BF... absent), and now holds 566,068.055810 USDC.inj (denom ibc/E107DB3E..., hash verified locally by sha256 recomputation against the proposal's claimed trace paths). The return exceeds the sent amount by exactly 1.000000 USDC. The proposal text states proceeds are 1:1 less gas/relayer fees, which would reduce rather than increase the amount, so the +1 USDC is an unexplained top-up — small, in the pool's favour, and not a loss. Transaction-level confirmation of the individual legs was not available (the LCD's tx-search endpoint is unimplemented), so reconciliation rests on the two pool balances.
remediation: No action required beyond the multisig publishing the transaction hashes for each migration leg in the forum thread, as the proposal promises, so the +1 USDC top-up is explained on the record.
title: USDC.n to USDC.inj migration reconciles, with a +1.000000 USDC difference

description: No pause, halt, or emergency message type exists in the governance parameters or in any audited proposal's messages on either chain. Yet the September 2026 Neutron incident was handled by validators halting the Cosmos Hub at block 33,086,740 and restarting on Gaia v28.3.0 with a one-time state change at height 33,086,741 that moved 1,227,121.374688 ATOM to a 4-of-6 recovery multisig — all before proposal 1058, which merely ratified the mandate afterwards. The recovery multisig itself is verified on-chain (LegacyAminoPubKey threshold 4 of 6; balance now 136,746 uatom, sequence 2), but the halt/restart authority that created it is uncodified social consensus among validators, not an on-chain power with a defined threshold or scope.
remediation: Codify emergency authority in a governance proposal: who may halt the chain, under what conditions, what state changes are permitted, and the deadline for retrospective ratification. Re-check: confirm a published emergency procedure exists in Hub documentation and that future halt events cite it.
title: Emergency powers are off-governance: chain halt and state change preceded the vote

amount_at_risk: Hub bonded 343.73M ATOM; Osmosis bonded 155.28M OSMO
description: Osmosis caps its active set at 30 validators (max_validators=30, verified in staking params); the top 4 hold 37.37% and the top 10 hold 60.77% of bonded stake (HHI 0.05570). On the Cosmos Hub (180 validators) the top 1 holds 19.03%, top 4 hold 38.15%, and top 10 hold 56.56% (HHI 0.05855). A coordinated top-4 set is close to a blocking minority on either chain, and on Osmosis only 30 entities share all validation.
remediation: Monitor top-N shares each quarter with this toolkit; consider raising Osmosis max_validators and reviewing Hub minimum-commission / delegation-program incentives that entrench the top set. Re-check: rerun fetch_treasury.py and compare validator_concentration top4/top10 shares.
title: Validator-set concentration is high on both chains

description: Delegation-weighted concentration over all fetched voters: Cosmos Hub 1061 (864 voters with stake) top-1 10.59%, top-4 26.34%, top-10 39.37%, HHI 0.02689, Gini 0.8779. Osmosis 1067 (494 voters) top-1 9.36%, top-4 31.18%, top-10 56.34%, HHI 0.03940, Gini 0.8968. Osmosis 1066 (503 voters) top-1 9.62%, top-4 32.05%, top-10 57.90%, HHI 0.04109, Gini 0.8998. The top 10 voters command a majority of the voting stake on Osmosis live votes. Stake is measured at fetch time (snapshot), not at vote time.
remediation: No on-chain fix is available from this finding alone; track the metric per proposal with this toolkit and flag any vote where the top-4 share exceeds the veto threshold (33.4%). Re-check: rerun audit_proposals.py while votes are live.
title: Voting-stake concentration in live votes is high (Gini ~0.88-0.90)

description: Osmosis community_tax is 0 and mint inflation is 0 (the mint endpoint returns Not Implemented; /osmosis/mint/v1beta1/inflation returns 0). Measured over 136,465 blocks the uosmo pool balance moved by only +0.506633 OSMO (63,780,813.94 OSMO at height 74,934,511). The pool is therefore funded by protocol revenue (e.g. taker fees), not by issuance or a staking-reward tax, so its sustainability depends on fee flow that is not visible in the governance parameters.
remediation: Document the pool's revenue sources and their recent rates in Osmosis documentation, so spend proposals can be sized against real inflow. Re-check: rerun fetch_treasury.py over a longer block span and compare bond_pool_change.
title: Osmosis community pool is static: no issuance or tax inflow in params

description: Proposal 1061 schedules the upgrade at height 33,935,300. At the measured average block interval of 5.68 s over the last 1,000 blocks, that height is reached about 496,336 s after the fetch, i.e. about 88,455 s (24.6 hours) after voting ends (2026-11-17T11:57:22Z). Combined with F-01 (no timelock), operators have under a day between a passing vote and a mandatory binary switch.
remediation: Schedule future upgrades at least one full voting period after the earliest possible passage, or add a post-passage delay (see F-01). Re-check: rerun audit_proposals.py and read proposals-cosmoshub.json timelock.voting_end_to_upgrade_seconds_estimate.
title: Gaia v29.1.0 upgrade executes about 24.6 hours after voting ends

description: Proposal 1066 ('Signal a 10% Minimum Validator Commission') contains no messages. Whatever the vote outcome, no parameter changes on-chain; a separate parameter-change proposal is required to enforce a minimum commission. The vote is a sentiment signal only, and its 99.28% yes share (54,167,741,349,405 yes of counted votes at fetch) does not itself change any rule.
remediation: None for the audit; a follow-up MsgUpdateParams-style proposal is needed if the signal is to be enforced. Re-check: look for a parameter-change proposal citing 1066.
title: Osmosis proposal 1066 is a non-binding signal with no executable message

description: At fetch time (height 33,847,852, 2026-11-12 18:30 UTC) proposal 1061 has 38.44% turnout against a 40% quorum, with 100.00% yes share of counted votes and 0 veto. Voting ends 2026-11-17T11:57:22Z, so the outcome is still open: if turnout does not reach 40%, the upgrade fails despite unanimous yes votes. This is a snapshot observation, not a weakness.
remediation: None; re-check after voting ends by rerunning audit_proposals.py.
title: Cosmos Hub proposal 1061 turnout is below quorum at the snapshot (vote still open)

description: Proposal 1057 (passed, turnout 66.35%, yes share 99.98%) sent 55,500,000,000,000 uosmo (55,500,000 OSMO) from the community pool to the burn address osmo1qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqmcn030.
